passage:
Bhavna's cousin's birthday party had moved to the terrace by ten. Someone passed round a vape, and Pranav, fifteen, felt every eye on him. "Don't be boring," a boy said. Pranav grinned, said "I'm the designated snack guard," grabbed the chips and went to the far corner. Nobody pushed further.

Near the stairs, an older boy with a sports bag was handing out free vapes and pills wrapped in foil to the younger ones. "Take one, bring your friends, we can sort out selling later," he said to Bhavna. Something in her stomach turned cold; it felt like bait. She shook her head, went down the stairs, and texted her aunt to pick her up. Her aunt arrived within twenty minutes.

Kamal, Pranav's friend, had been quiet all evening. Pranav noticed Kamal's hands shaking and remembered that Kamal had been using something almost every weekend for months. He didn't lecture. He said, "I'm worried about you, and I'll come with you to talk to your sister," and Kamal, staring at the floor, said maybe.

That night, Pranav lay awake thinking he was curious about it too, but that curiosity and wanting to look cool were tangled, and he wanted to read what it really does to a growing brain first.

qa.q: What did Pranav say to get out of the pressure at the party?
qa.a: He said he was the designated snack guard and took the chips to the far corner.

qa.q: How is the older boy's offer to Bhavna different from the pressure Pranav felt from the boy who called him boring?
qa.a: The boy calling Pranav boring wanted him to join in, while the older boy offered free items as a hook to bring Bhavna and her friends into selling. Pranav could joke his way out, whereas Bhavna needed to leave and tell an adult.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling as he lay awake that night?
qa.a: He felt curious but unsure, aware that some of his interest came from wanting to look cool, so he wanted facts before deciding.

qa.q: What could Pranav do next for Kamal if Kamal keeps using and gets worse?
qa.a: He could keep showing care without lecturing, encourage Kamal to accept help, and tell a trusted adult if Kamal's safety is at risk.

grounding: One party is used to show a friend-group offer, an older peer's hook, personal curiosity and a friend's protective concern about the same subject.
